title: Opposition Leaders Embrace Modi's 'Dimagi Naxal' Label After Independence Day Speech
excerpt: PM Modi's warning against "ideological Naxals" in his Red Fort address triggered a political firestorm, with Congress's Chidambaram, PDP's Mehbooba Mufti, and AAP's Kejriwal turning the remark into a badge of honor.
body:
• PM Modi warned against "dimagi Naxals" — ideological Naxals — during his 80th Independence Day speech from the Red Fort on August 15
  • Congress leader P. Chidambaram declared he was "proud to be a dimagi Naxal," while PDP's Mehbooba Mufti and AAP's Kejriwal also embraced the label
  • Union Minister Kiren Rijiju clarified the term targeted supporters of Maoists and separatists, not opposition leaders — a claim Congress dismissed
  • The CJP's Instagram handle was briefly taken down on Independence Day before being restored, adding to the social media dimension of the political clash

Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Independence Day speech from the Red Fort on Friday sparked one of the sharpest political exchanges of 2026, after he warned the nation to "isolate" those he called "dimagi Naxals" — a Hindi term roughly translating to "ideological Naxals" or "intellectual Maoists."

Within hours, opposition leaders across party lines had seized the phrase and turned it into a rallying cry against the ruling BJP.

Chidambaram: 'Proud to Be a Dimagi Naxal'

Senior Congress leader and former Union Home Minister P. Chidambaram was among the first to respond, declaring he was "proud to be a dimagi Naxal," according to the Economic Times. The statement set the tone for a broader opposition pushback.

Congress swiftly framed Modi's remark as a sign of political desperation. "This is a sure sign of his desperation," Congress said in its rebuttal, according to the Times of India, accusing the prime minister of using the Independence Day platform to target political opponents rather than address the nation's concerns.

Congress MP Pawan Khera also pushed back against BJP attempts to clarify the remark, insisting it was clearly aimed at opposition voices.

Mehbooba Mufti Joins the Chorus

PDP leader and former Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Mehbooba Mufti escalated the defiance further. "I support Article 370. I'm a dimaagi Naxal," Mufti said, according to the Economic Times, explicitly linking her support for Kashmir's revoked special status to the label Modi had deployed.

Her response broadened the scope of the political fallout, tying the dimagi Naxal debate to unresolved questions about federalism, regional autonomy, and the BJP's approach to Jammu and Kashmir.

Rijiju's Damage Control

Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju attempted to contain the controversy on August 16, insisting that Modi's remark was not aimed at opposition leaders.

"Only those who support Maoists and separatists are 'dimagi Naxals,'" Rijiju said, according to the Economic Times. He specified that the term targeted supporters of Maoist ideology and separatism, not legitimate political opposition.

Congress rejected the clarification outright. BJP spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi followed up on August 17, questioning Congress's position by contrasting Chidambaram's defiant embrace of the label with former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh's 2006 assessment that Naxalism was India's "gravest internal security threat."

"Have to isolate dimagi Naxals."

— PM Narendra Modi, Independence Day speech, August 15, 2026

The Social Media Dimension

The political clash unfolded against a backdrop of heightened social media tensions. The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), the satirical youth-led movement that has organized protests over NEET exam paper leaks and demanded Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, saw its Instagram handle briefly taken down on Independence Day before being restored.

"Attempt to muzzle our voice on Independence Day," the CJP said, according to the Times of India. The episode added fuel to an already charged atmosphere, with opposition leaders accusing the government of using both rhetoric and platform control to silence dissent.

AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal, who has positioned himself as a champion of the student protest movement and has repeatedly clashed with Modi over the NEET crisis, joined the chorus of opposition leaders pushing back against the dimagi Naxal framing. Kejriwal has been at the forefront of defending Gen Z protesters and accusing the Modi government of heavy-handed tactics against young demonstrators.

What's Next

The dimagi Naxal exchange is likely to reverberate through the monsoon session of Parliament. With the opposition alliance already energized by the student protest movement and the BJP defending its governance record ahead of 2029 general elections, the rhetorical battle lines are hardening.

For the estimated 4.5 million Indian-Americans and NRIs worldwide, the exchange dominated social media feeds over the weekend, offering a window into the deepening polarization of Indian politics — and the increasingly blurred line between political rhetoric and protest movements.
